text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Syria won't budge on terms for talks
- Ex-Justice Minister Yaacov Ne'eman denies charges at start of trial
- Lawyer Dan Avi-Yitzhak questioned secretly in Bar-On case - report
- Cabinet approves Elyakim Rubenstein as attorney general
- Hamas activist Mousa Abu Marzook to be extradited to Israel
HAARETZ
- Elyakim Rubenstein to enter attorney general office without polygraph test
- Michael Eitan: If I am not appointed as science minister I will consider that the end of my career
- Cabinet approves increasing defence budget by 300 million shekels
- Justice minister, knesset members to be questioned soon
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Police continued investigation in corruption case secretly
MAARIV
- Internal Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani demands director general of prime minister's office Avigdor Liberman apologise for comments about police
- Syrian President Hafez Assad demands good will gesture from Netanyahu before renewing talks
- Summer time to be shortened from 220 days to 175 on request of religious parties
GLOBES
- Customs head: "conditional exemptions" on imports to be cancelled in coming months
- Offers in foreign currency weaken
- Government approves reduction in discounts on municipal taxes, privatisation of administration of public housing
